base.zverev_straight_set_estimate: From base rates alone, P(Zverev 2-0) is about 42%, with a plausible range of 37-47%. Our model says 38.9%, so base rates sit about 3 points higher. What pushes it up: generic 60-68% favourites win 2-0 about 42-45% of the time (n=449 and n=1,244; smoothed value at the market's 64.2% is 42.2-42.5%). In elite matchups 73-76% of favourite wins come in straight sets, against 64-69% for generic favourites; Zverev himself won 70% of his wins 2-0 (35/50), 76% as favourite against top-20 opponents, and 8 of 12 against players ranked 5-15. Multiplying the market's 64.2% by a 73% straight-set share gives about 47%. What pulls it down: 5 of the last 6 hard meetings with de Minaur went to a deciding set and Zverev won 0 of those 6 in straights (his only 2-0 wins were in 2018-19). Zverev went 3 sets in 2 of 3 matches this week with an ankle problem, and 5 of 9 since July. On a 58.6% win chance, as our model has it, the generic base rate is about 37-38%, which matches the model. So the model's 2-0 number is reasonable for its own win probability; the gap comes from the model's lower win chance, which rests on the -8 point ankle adjustment. The crowd is right that Zverev 2-0 is the single most likely result, but it still happens less than half the time. If P(Zverev 2-0) is about 42%, de Minaur +1.5 sets is about 58% (fair price about -138). That is below the 59.7% break-even at -148, so the pick is roughly break-even or slightly negative on base rates and is only positive if you accept the model's 61.1%. The search-reported NEO.bet price for 'de Minaur to win a set' (1.57, 63.7% raw) would put Zverev 2-0 near 36-40%, closer to our model.
base.adf_gea_straight_set_estimate: From base rates alone, P(either player wins 2-0) in QF-A is about 60%, range 57-65%, so P(3 sets) is about 40%. Split: ADF 2-0 about 31-32%, Gea 2-0 about 29-30% (with ADF a slight market favourite near 53%). Our model has 61.6% (ADF 31.4%, Gea 30.2%), which is consistent. Inputs: tour near-coin-flip matches end 2-0 in 58.1% (ratings-calibrated) to 61.6% (rank-based) of cases, and all hard Bo3 in 64.1%. ADF's matches ended 2-0 in 69.0% (n=58, 2025-26) but only 61.9% in 2026 (n=21). Gea's ended 2-0 in 50% (n=12, too thin to weight much). This week Gea and ADF each went 3 sets twice (2/4 and 2/3). The search-reported Oddset '3 sets' price of 2.25 (44.4% raw) puts either-2-0 at about 56% or higher. Gea +1.5 sets on base rates is about 67-69%, against the model's 68.6%, so it is consistent but leaves little room at -202 (66.9% break-even). Separate flag: the 'No tiebreak' value pick (model 61.8%) is not supported by base rates. ADF (48%, n=64) and Gea (58%, n=12) both play tiebreaks more often than the tour's 40.5%, and 9 of 12 of the four players' matches this week had a tiebreak. Base rates put No tiebreak at about 50-55%, below the 60.3% needed at -152.
base.summary:
I checked the straight-sets question against our local match data: tour-level hard-court best-of-3 matches from 2023-01 to 2026-09, plus this week's Shanghai rows. Retirements and walkovers are excluded, and Laver Cup, Next Gen and Davis Cup are left out. Two gaps: 2026 Canada is missing, and the Shanghai 2026 rows have no opponent ranks. Scripts and intermediate files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ReadME/466937d5-7a1a-5b7b-8d33-791a10f066e2/scratchpad/wf_tmp/ (br_common.py, t1.py to t8.py, df.pkl, bt_p.pkl). I did not fetch anything from the web.

QF-B: the crowd's 'Zverev 2-0' is the single most likely set score in base rates as well as in our model, but it is still less likely than not. Base rates put it at about 42% (range 37-47%) against our 38.9%. Pushing it up: elite matchups produce fewer 3-setters (about 30-32% against 36% tour-wide). Zverev wins in straight sets often (70% of his wins since Oct 2024; 8 of 12 against players ranked 5-15). Generic 64% favourites win 2-0 about 42-45% of the time. Pulling it down: de Minaur took 5 of the last 6 hard-court meetings to a deciding set, and Zverev has not beaten him 2-0 since 2019. Zverev also went 3 sets in 2 of 3 matches this week with the ankle problem. Our model's 2-0 number fits its own 58.6% win chance; the difference from the market comes from the lower win chance, which leans on the ankle adjustment. Consequence: the high-hit pick de Minaur +1.5 sets is about 58% on base rates against 61.1% in the model, which makes it roughly break-even at -148 rather than clearly positive. It should be presented as model-dependent (ankle) rather than research-confirmed, or taken only at about -135 or better. The de Minaur moneyline value pick likewise depends on the model's win probability; base rates do not test it directly.

QF-A: base rates say about 60% that one player wins 2-0 (ADF about 31%, Gea about 29%), against the model's 61.6% (31.4% / 30.2%). That is consistent, and Gea +1.5 sets (base rate about 67-69%, model 68.6%) holds up, but with little margin at -202. The main new problem is the 'No tiebreak' value pick. Model 61.8% looks too high: ADF plays tiebreaks in 48% of his matches (n=64) and Gea in 58% (n=12, thin), against 40.5% tour-wide, and 9 of 12 of the four players' matches this week had a tiebreak. Base rates put No tiebreak at about 50-55%, below the 60.3% needed at -152, so I would drop it or downgrade it.

Caveats: Gea has only 12 hard best-of-3 tour-level matches in local data plus 6 Slam matches, not the 14 in the brief, and no Challengers. Some H2H set scores (2018-19 Zverev 2-0 wins, Vienna 2021, Laver Cup 2026) are taken from CONTEXT rather than local data. Two of Zverev's eight H2H wins have no score in either source. Market figures (NEO.bet 1.57, Oddset 2.25) are search-reported from CONTEXT and were not opened by me.

research.tally: 33 distinct sources, plus 2 prediction markets and 1 fan poll. None picks de Minaur to win outright; Stats Insider backs him only as a value bet. 18 sources make a set-level call: 7 say Zverev 2-0, 5 say Zverev 2-1 (Zverev wins, de Minaur takes a set), and 6 say 3 sets / de Minaur wins at least one set without naming a winner. So 11 of 18 expect de Minaur to win a set. Only 2 of the 7 Zverev 2-0 calls come from human tipsters (bets.com.au, LWOS). The other 5 are algorithm sites printing their single most likely score (ATS.io, Agatha, Foretennis, Forebet, Predixsport at 44.4%). Of 13 human set-level calls, 2 say Zverev 2-0 and 11 say de Minaur wins a set. About 13 more sources give a winner only, all Zverev, and several of those add 'over 22.5 games' or 'not a smooth match' (Sportwetten24, Predictobets, bet365 DE, Tuze). Model sites put Zverev at 59-74% (Forebet 59, Stats Insider 62, Court Shark 62, Agatha 64, Foretennis 64, Tennis.com 65, ATS 71, Predixsport 74; mean about 65%). More importantly, the books already price the crowd's view. Zverev 2-0 trades at 2.10-2.30 (break-even 43.5-47.6%), which is at or above any honest estimate, so every Zverev-side price we found has negative EV at 43% and 64%. The de Minaur ML 'value' and most of the de Minaur +1.5 edge come from one assumption: a 50% chance Zverev is limited, worth 16 points of win probability when he is. Run the model at the market's win probability and the de Minaur bets go to about break-even or worse. Only 2 pick ADF 2-0, and both are algorithmic aggregators (Oddspedia algorithm, Forebet 51%).
